evidence_quotes.quote: En este marco, el presente artículo busca caracterizar la problemática de los servicios desvinculados de agua y cloacas que operan en el amba.

El marco regulatorio habilita la construcción y operación de servicios desvinculados previa autorización de la autoridad de aplicación, quien tiene que responder dentro de un plazo de 90 días, prorrogables por un periodo igual.
los criterios de priorización establecidos por AySA no contemplan los problemas de calidad registrados por el eras, ya que refieren solo a la proximidad de los barrios al área servida
La estimación de los servicios desvinculados consideró la información del eras (2022), un informe realizado por la Universidad Nacional de San Antonio de Areco (2022) y relevamiento en campo.
Este trabajo relevó 365 servicios desvinculados, que posibilitan el acceso de aproximadamente 498 483 personas en 21 de los municipios

del universo que audita el eras, el 46 % carece de servicios de cloración (122), el 30 % da cuenta de la contaminación fisicoquímica a través de la presencia de nitratos (80) y el 20 % presenta contaminación bacteriológica (48)

criterion_notes.c1: Examines household and neighborhood drinking-water and sewerage service access in the Metropolitan Area of Buenos Aires (AMBA), focusing on decentralized 'unlinked' (servicios desvinculados) water supply and sewage systems operating within the concession territory of the state utility AySA.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading of Criterion 2. Plain reading: examines legal, regulatory, institutional, and governance frameworks governing metropolitan and peri-urban water and sanitation services in AMBA. Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: directly examines (1) utility ownership and regulatory structure governing service access (state concessionaire AySA under Law 26.221 and Resolution 170/2010 vs. five decentralized ownership/operation regimes: formal cooperatives/mutuals with legal personality, neighborhood associations/consortia, municipal operators, private operators, and unoperated systems), (2) regulatory authorization and definitional screening rules (90-day authorization requirement under Law 26.221; ERAS's operator-and-billing definition that excludes unoperated neighborhood systems from regulatory registration and auditing), and (3) eligibility/prioritization rules for utility network incorporation (AySA's expansion prioritization rules restrict incorporation to proximity to the served area and water-supply feasibility while excluding ERAS-documented water-quality hazards).
criterion_notes.c3: Empirical qualitative and descriptive study based on primary fieldwork conducted in 2022-2023 (15 in-depth interviews with officials from ERAS, APLA, SSRH, AySA, municipal actors, and residents; technical site visits; field mapping of 365 unlinked systems) combined with legal/documentary analysis and secondary data from INDEC (2022) and ERAS (2022) regulatory water-quality audits.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports municipality-level household piped water and sewerage coverage (Table 1), number of unlinked systems and population served across 21 municipalities (365 systems serving 498,483 residents, Table 3) disaggregated by operational governance model (Figures 1-2), service quality and sanitation failures (46% without chlorination, 30% nitrate contamination, 20% bacteriological contamination among 264 ERAS-audited systems; sewer overflows and non-functioning treatment plants), and exclusion from formal AySA network integration.
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies population and units of analysis (365 unlinked neighborhood systems serving ~498,483 inhabitants across 21 AMBA municipalities, 264 ERAS-audited systems, municipal household coverage across 26 jurisdictions, and 15 key informants), legal/institutional exposures, service access/quality/exclusion outcomes, and qualitative/mixed-source exploratory case study design.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish with English and Portuguese titles and abstracts. Eligible under Criterion 10 because direct comprehension/translation from the provided Spanish full text is fully feasible (screened directly from Spanish text by AI screener; translation method and translator to be logged in extraction_note during data extraction).

study_design: Exploratory and descriptive qualitative case study combining legal/documentary analysis, secondary census and regulatory audit statistics, 15 in-depth key-informant interviews, technical site visits, and field mapping
population_and_sample: 365 decentralized 'unlinked' water and sanitation systems (servicios desvinculados) serving approximately 498,483 inhabitants across 21 municipalities in the Metropolitan Area of Buenos Aires (AMBA), Argentina (within AySA's concession territory; plus 264 ERAS-audited systems, 2022 census household data across 26 AMBA jurisdictions, and 15 key-informant interviewees)
exposure: Regulatory classification, authorization, auditing, and network-incorporation rules under Law 26.221, Resolution 170/2010, ERAS, APLA, and AySA (including ERAS's operator-billing definitional requirement and AySA's proximity and supply-feasibility prioritization criteria), alongside decentralized service ownership/operational models (neighborhood organization/consortium, formal cooperative/mutual, municipal, private, and unoperated systems)
outcome: Household piped water and sewer coverage across AMBA municipalities; population accessing water and sanitation via unlinked systems (498,483 residents across 365 systems by operator type); service quality and infrastructure maintenance outcomes (46% lacking chlorination, 30% nitrate contamination, and 20% bacteriological contamination among 264 ERAS-audited systems; sewage overflows and treatment plant obsolescence); and exclusion from incorporation into AySA's formal utility network
rationale: Empirical qualitative and field-mapping study of decentralized 'unlinked' drinking-water and sewerage systems (servicios desvinculados) in the Metropolitan Area of Buenos Aires, Argentina. Satisfies all inclusion criteria under both the plain and narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type readings of Criterion 2: it examines concrete statutory, regulatory, ownership, and utility-incorporation rules governing service access and quality (Law 26.221, Resolution 170/2010, ERAS operator-based registration/auditing rules, AySA's proximity- and feasibility-based network incorporation criteria, and cooperative/neighborhood/municipal/private/unoperated governance structures) and links them empirically (15 interviews, technical visits, field survey of 365 systems serving 498,483 people, INDEC census data, and ERAS audits of 264 systems) to access, service quality, sanitation failure, and exclusion from formal utility integration. Spanish full text is eligible under Criterion 10 as translation is directly feasible.
